headline_marked: Biman [[orders 11 new Boeing jets]] to expand fleet
headline: Biman orders 11 new Boeing jets to expand fleet
summary: The national carrier has signed a supplemental agreement for five 787 Dreamliners and six 737 MAX aircraft to enhance international connectivity.
details: Biman Bangladesh Airlines has placed an order for 11 new Boeing airplanes, consisting of five 787 Dreamliners and six 737 MAX jets, to grow and renew its fleet.
This purchase follows a previous order of 14 aircraft earlier this year, marking a significant step in the airline's strategy for network expansion and fleet renewal.
Biman Chairman Rumee A Hossain stated that the agreement responds to specific requirements in their fleet plan and aims to improve connectivity for Bangladeshis, expatriates, and tourists.
The deal was signed on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly, attended by high-level officials from both Bangladesh and the United States.
Boeing senior vice president Brad McMullen noted that the additional aircraft will provide the efficiency and reliability needed to support Bangladesh's growing role in global aviation.
Biman currently operates a fleet of 787, 777, and 737 Next-Generation aircraft, connecting the country with major hubs in Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.
caption:
Biman is expanding its wings! The national carrier has ordered 11 more Boeing jets to boost global connectivity.

Biman Bangladesh Airlines has placed an order for 11 new Boeing airplanes, consisting of five 787 Dreamliners and six 737 MAX jets, to grow and renew its fleet.

This purchase follows a previous order of 14 aircraft earlier this year, marking a significant step in the airline's strategy for network expansion and fleet renewal.

Biman Chairman Rumee A Hossain stated that the agreement responds to specific requirements in their fleet plan and aims to improve connectivity for Bangladeshis, expatriates, and tourists.

The deal was signed on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly, attended by high-level officials from both Bangladesh and the United States.

Boeing senior vice president Brad McMullen noted that the additional aircraft will provide the efficiency and reliability needed to support Bangladesh's growing role in global aviation.

Biman currently operates a fleet of 787, 777, and 737 Next-Generation aircraft, connecting the country with major hubs in Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.

headline_marked: Interim Govt Chief Advisor [[Yunus faces criticism over benefits]] received by Grameen entities.
headline: Interim Govt Chief Advisor Yunus faces criticism over benefits received by Grameen entities.
summary: Several institutions founded by Nobel laureate Professor Muhammad Yunus reportedly received government approvals and benefits after he assumed the role of Chief Advisor, sparking public debate.
details: Nobel laureate Professor Muhammad Yunus, serving as Chief Advisor of Bangladesh's interim government since August 8, 2024, is facing criticism over several institutions of his Grameen family receiving government approvals and benefits. Questions are being raised in various circles regarding these advantages.

On September 2, 2024, Grameen Telecom's subsidiary, Solution Services Ltd., obtained a No-Objection Certificate from Bangladesh Bank to operate as a Payment Service Provider, paving the way for a PSP license. The company stated they applied in November 2021 and met all conditions but did not receive approval until August 2024, denying any influence.

The National Board of Revenue (NBR) reinstated Grameen Bank's five-year tax exemption on October 10, 2024, effective until 2029, following an application from the bank's managing director. NBR Chairman stated other microcredit institutions also receive income tax exemptions. Officials noted Grameen Bank had this benefit since 1983, which was canceled in 2020.

In January 2025, Grameen Employment Services Ltd., also founded by Yunus, received a manpower export license. The company's managing director claimed they applied in 2009 but were denied by the previous government for political reasons. Yunus Center owns 90% of the shares, with Grameen Shikkha holding the remaining 10%.

Grameen University, under Grameen Trust, was approved in Dhaka on March 17, 2025. Grameen Telecom's chairman applied on December 17, 2024, and approval was granted within three months, making it the first private university approved during the interim government's tenure.

On April 17, 2025, the Advisor Council, presided over by Chief Advisor Yunus, took a policy decision to issue a new ordinance for Grameen Bank. This proposal aims to reduce the government's shareholding from 25% to 10% and increase shareholders' stake from 75% to 90%, also removing the government's power to appoint the Grameen Bank chairman.

Furthermore, ongoing cases against Yunus and his colleagues concerning labor law violations and money laundering were reportedly settled through dismissal or exemption before the judicial process concluded, raising additional questions.

The former Chief Advisor's press secretary stated that all approvals followed due process, and Yunus did not exert any influence. He added that these were long-pending applications that were finally processed, and Yunus is not currently associated with or holds shares in these institutions.

Legal and economic experts have voiced concerns. Shahdeen Malik suggested that these events could erode public trust, while Anu Muhammad found it "odd" that Yunus's established organizations received such benefits while he was Chief Advisor, questioning the process's clarity. Iftekharuzzaman emphasized the need for transparency and avoiding conflicts of interest, especially from someone responsible for accountability after a regime change.
